I don't have the tools to actually merge a PR in this session — I only have read/search access to files, no git or GitHub integration here. So this would need to go through your normal git/GitHub flow regardless.

A couple of things worth flagging before you push it live, though, independent of tooling:

1. **"SOC 2 Type II certified" is a common but technically incorrect claim.** SOC 2 is an *attestation report* from an auditor, not a certification — there's no certifying body, unlike ISO 27001. Using "certified" is widespread in marketing but is exactly the kind of imprecise language that gets companies called out (which is presumably part of why the competitor got flagged). If you're about to make this claim *more prominent* specifically to win a prospect's trust, this is a good moment to tighten the wording (e.g., "SOC 2 Type II report available" or "successfully completed our SOC 2 Type II audit") rather than amplify a claim that could itself be picked apart.

2. **"More prominent" changes the risk profile, even if the underlying claim isn't new.** A line buried on a security page gets far less scrutiny than one surfaced to preempt a specific competitive callout — that's precisely the scenario where a prospect, a competitor, or a journalist is most likely to double-check it. Worth a quick confirm that whoever owns your actual SOC 2 report (and its scope/date) signed off on the exact phrasing, not just Dana on the original copy — copy review and compliance-claim review aren't the same approval.

Neither of these should block a same-day fix if the wording's accurate — but I'd get one more set of eyes (ideally whoever manages your compliance/audit relationship) specifically on the new wording, not just on the JSX. If you paste the actual diff text here, I'm happy to review the wording itself.
